_comment: Shared cases for hiding sessions that have gone quiet (#547, #619).
The threshold is a preference, so the rule stays client-side (ADR-0011) and is
Three details that are easy to get wrong and all matter: the clock is
`last_seen_at` and not the status, so a `working` session whose reports stopped
is hidden too — the same 'nothing is happening here' signal; an unreadable
timestamp keeps the session visible, because losing a row over a date that will
not parse is worse than showing one row too many; and the comparison is strictly
greater than, so a session exactly at the threshold is still shown.
`presets` is the list of steps the settings screen offers, in its order.

cases.why: a threshold of zero is off — nothing is ever hidden by it
quieter than the threshold, so hidden
a `working` session whose reports stopped is hidden too — the clock is last_seen_at, not the status
and a recent `ended` one is not hidden by this rule, which is not the hide-ended preference
exactly at the threshold is still shown — the comparison is strict
one second past it is hidden
a timestamp that will not parse keeps the row rather than losing it
no timestamp at all keeps the row for the same reason
a timestamp in the future is not quiet
